verdicts.reason: All five original findings (RV-01..RV-05) are closed, and minimality, format, traceability and inheritance boundaries pass. But the r02 fix introduced a new contract-level conflict in design.md:3862: the clause 'whole-DB artifact vs protected tables (exclude schemas OR restore into an isolated DB then root-controlled switchover)' contradicts the fixed target semantics at design.md:3864 (live verified DSN), :3866 (same verified artifact/target) and :3870 (same no-follow fd), grants root a new direct data-movement write path that violates 'root must not execute in place of the executor', and relies on an undefined 'identity/recovery tables' scope that cannot hold simultaneously with a whole-DB restore of a database where account data and recovery_runs share one PostgreSQL fault domain (design.md:545, :1718). ADR-0031:1036 mirrors this as an unpassable release gate. gap-map section 2.5 requires a security review PASS, so neither design nor security can pass.

items.title: design.md:3862 new artifact/protected-table boundary clause conflicts with the fixed restore target contract and adds a root write path
items.fact: New sentence: 'whole-DB artifact vs these protected tables (exclude the corresponding schemas OR restore into an isolated DB then root-controlled switchover) is also fixed by the approval record.' Conflicts: (1) :3864 passes only the live verified DSN as target_connection, :3866 requires the child to restore the same verified artifact/target and root to verify 'the same target', :3870 requires the same no-follow stable fd -- an isolated-DB staging plus root switchover breaks all three; (2) :3862 says root does not execute in place of the executor and ADR :1007 limits root to lock/drain/exclusive/Begin/binding/audit/VerifyRestored, so root-controlled data movement is a new privileged write path; (3) 'identity/recovery tables' is undefined (0 hits for the term, no table enumeration) while design.md:545 places account data and recovery metadata in one PostgreSQL fault domain and :1718 puts recovery_runs/recovery_restore_bindings in the same Store, so a whole-DB artifact necessarily contains both, making the role-scope prohibition and a real restore mutually unsatisfiable; excluding those schemas leaves source_schema_digest/restored_schema_digest semantics undefined (:3860, :3866). ADR :1036 mirrors the prohibition as a release gate.
items.impact: Production stays closed (no live exposure), but the normative contract line is self-contradictory, the ADR release gate :1036 cannot be satisfied by a genuine whole-DB restore, and the untracked isolated-DB/root-switchover option contradicts ADR :977 'does not rewrite or weaken the existing restore software contract'.
items.recommendation: Fix this round: (1) replace 'identity/recovery tables' with an enumerable list (recovery_runs, recovery_restore_bindings, audit tables) and state that account/business tables are written by the restore itself as a legitimate write surface; (2) delete or demote the isolated-DB plus root-switchover option (move to a separate decision, updating :3864/:3866/:3870 target semantics if kept); (3) if schema exclusion is kept, replace 'whole-DB artifact' with 'single verified artifact whose schema scope is fixed by the approval record' and define both schema digests; (4) align framework.md:1036 accordingly.
items.disposition: must fix this round; blocking for both design PASS and security PASS
